card.title: Linear momentum
card.says: a **vector** measuring how hard it is to stop a moving object: its mass $m$ times its velocity $\vec{v}$, pointing in the same direction as $\vec{v}$.
card.from: Newton's original form of the second law, $\sum\vec{F} = \dfrac{\Delta\vec{p}}{\Delta t}$: net force is the rate of change of momentum.
card.useWhen: objects collide, rebound, explode, or receive a brief push—always pick a positive direction first so opposite velocities carry opposite signs.
card.example: A $4\text{ kg}$ bowling ball rolling right at $+5\text{ m/s}$ has $p = 4(+5) = +20\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. A $0.5\text{ kg}$ ball flying left at $-40\text{ m/s}$ has $p = 0.5(-40) = -20\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$ — same magnitude, opposite direction.
card.analogy: A slow freight train and a fast ball are both hard to stop for different reasons—momentum combines mass and velocity into one quantity with a direction.
